question: Which of these festivals commemorates the resurrection of Jesus from the dead?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Easter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Easter** is a Christian festival that celebrates the **resurrection of Jesus Christ** from the dead, as described in the New Testament of the Bible.
 
• The event is considered the **foundation of Christian faith**, as it signifies the triumph of Jesus over death and his role as the savior of humanity.
 
• Easter marks the end of the **Lenten season**, a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance observed by Christians.
 
• The date of Easter varies each year as it is celebrated on the first Sunday following the **first full moon** on or after the spring equinox (March 21).
 
• It is often associated with various traditions, such as the **Easter egg**, which symbolizes new life, and the Easter bunny, which is linked to fertility and springtime.
 
• Easter is preceded by Holy Week, which includes important days such as **Good Friday** (commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus) and **Holy Saturday**.
 
• It is celebrated worldwide by Christians with church services, feasts, and cultural traditions, emphasizing the themes of **renewal, hope, and salvation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Good Friday**__

 __
 
• **Good Friday** is observed to commemorate the **crucifixion of Jesus Christ** and his death at Calvary.
 
• It is marked as a solemn day of mourning and reflection in Christianity, usually falling on the Friday before Easter Sunday.
 
• Church services on Good Friday often include the **Stations of the Cross**, veneration of the cross, and readings from the Gospel.
 
 
 
• **New Year**__
 __
 
• **New Year** is a global celebration marking the beginning of a **new calendar year**, based on the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It is celebrated on **January 1** with festivities, fireworks, and resolutions for personal growth and improvement.
 
 
 
• **Christmas**__
 
 
• **Christmas** is celebrated on **December 25** to commemorate the **birth of Jesus Christ**.
 
• It is one of the most significant festivals in Christianity and is associated with traditions such as **gift-giving, decorating Christmas trees, and attending church services.**
